2027-04-21.title: Fourth Wednesday of Resurrection

readings: A priest according to the order of Melchizedek
2027-04-21.alt: Season of the Resurrection (Qyamta). In the Latin calendar today is the memorial of St Anselm, bishop and doctor of the Church.
2027-04-21.verse: Without father, without mother, without genealogy, having neither beginning of days nor end of life, but resembling the Son of God, he remains a priest forever.
theo: The Letter to the Hebrews reaches back to one of the most mysterious figures of the Old Testament. In Genesis 14 Abram returns from rescuing his nephew Lot, and a stranger comes out to meet him: “And King Melchizedek of Salem brought out bread and wine; he was priest of God Most High.” He blesses Abram, and Abram gives him a tenth of everything. Then Melchizedek vanishes from the story. Centuries later Psalm 110 speaks of a king whom God has sworn to make “a priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek.” Hebrews brings these two passages together and sees in them a portrait of Christ. Melchizedek's name means “king of righteousness”; he is king of Salem, that is, “king of peace”. Scripture gives him no father or mother, no genealogy, no birth or death: “resembling the Son of God, he remains a priest forever.” The writer does not say Melchizedek was an angel or a ghost. He says that Scripture's silence about his origin and end makes him a living picture of the true Priest, who has no beginning as the eternal Son and no end as the Risen One.

Then the letter argues, in the careful way of a rabbi, that this priesthood is greater than the priesthood of Levi. Abraham, the father of the whole people and the one who “had received the promises”, received a blessing from Melchizedek and gave him tithes: “It is beyond dispute that the inferior is blessed by the superior.” Levi, still unborn, was in a sense in Abraham and paid tithes through him. Then comes a line that rings with Easter: “In the one case, tithes are received by those who are mortal; in the other, by one of whom it is testified that he lives.” The Levitical priests died one after another, and their office passed from father to son. Christ's priesthood does not pass to anyone, for, as the same chapter says a little later, “he holds his priesthood permanently, because he continues forever. Consequently he is able for all time to save those who approach God through him, since he always lives to make intercession for them.” The Resurrection is not only the end of Christ's suffering; it is the beginning of his eternal priesthood. At this moment the Risen Lord stands before the Father, interceding for us. The Fathers of the Church loved to point out that Melchizedek brought out bread and wine. In every Holy Qurbana the eternal Priest offers himself under those same signs; our priests stand at the altar not in their own name but in his.

In the Gospel Jesus answers those who challenged him for healing on the sabbath. He speaks of witnesses, as in a court of law: the Law required two or three witnesses before a charge could stand. “If I testify about myself, my testimony is not true.” So he calls his witnesses. First John the Baptist: “He was a burning and shining lamp, and you were willing to rejoice for a while in his light.” Then a greater witness: “The works that the Father has given me to complete, the very works that I am doing, testify on my behalf that the Father has sent me.” And behind the works, the Father himself: “And the Father who sent me has himself testified on my behalf.” Jesus is not seeking his own glory: “I seek to do not my own will but the will of him who sent me.” The Church reads this passage in Easter time because the Resurrection is the Father's great testimony to his Son. When the Father raised Jesus from the dead, he declared before the whole world that this was his Son. The apostles then became witnesses in their turn, and so must we. The world will not believe because we argue well; it believes when it sees the works that the Risen Lord still does through his Church.
conn: “And King Melchizedek of Salem brought out bread and wine; he was priest of God Most High” (Genesis 14:18).
“The LORD has sworn and will not change his mind, ‘You are a priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek’” (Psalm 110:4), quoted in Hebrews 5:6 and 7:17.

Christ “holds his priesthood permanently, because he continues forever” (Hebrews 7:24–25); “It is Christ Jesus, who died, yes, who was raised, who is at the right hand of God, who indeed intercedes for us” (Romans 8:34).
“Only on the evidence of two or three witnesses shall a charge be sustained” (Deuteronomy 19:15); Jesus says the same in John 8:17–18.
John the Baptist “came as a witness to testify to the light” (John 1:7); he said, “He must increase, but I must decrease” (John 3:30).
At the Jordan a voice from heaven said, “This is my Son, the Beloved” (Matthew 3:17); in the Resurrection the Father declared Jesus Son of God with power (Romans 1:4).
altar: The Qurbana is the offering of the Priest according to the order of Melchizedek: bread and wine brought to the altar become, by the power of the Holy Spirit, the Body and Blood of the Risen Lord, who lives forever to intercede for us.
Our priests act in the person of Christ; there is one Priest and one Sacrifice, made present on every altar of the world.

live: Pray today by name for the priest who baptised you and for your parish priest.
When you cannot find words in prayer, say: Lord Jesus, you always live to intercede for me; pray for me now.
Give God the first part of the day: begin it with prayer before your phone.
Let one good work this week point beyond yourself to Christ, as John the Baptist did.
fathers: In the priest Melchizedek we see the mystery of the Lord's sacrifice prefigured: he offered bread and wine and blessed Abraham. Who is more a priest of the Most High than our Lord Jesus Christ, who offered to God the Father the very same thing Melchizedek had offered, bread and wine, that is, his Body and Blood?

Who is the king of righteousness, the king of peace, without beginning of days or end of life, if not Christ? Melchizedek received Abraham with bread and wine; so the sacraments of the Church are older than the synagogue, and the figure came before the law.
magis: The Church sees in the gesture of the king-priest Melchizedek, who brought out bread and wine, a prefiguring of her own offering.

Everything that the priesthood of the Old Covenant prefigured finds its fulfilment in Christ, the one high priest after the order of Melchizedek; the ministerial priesthood shares in his one priesthood.
Christ, the high priest of the good things to come, always lives to make intercession for those who draw near to God through him.
The signs worked by Jesus attest that the Father has sent him; they invite belief in him.
St John the Baptist is the Lord's immediate precursor, sent to prepare his way; he is more than a prophet.
saints: Latin calendar: St Anselm (1033–1109), born at Aosta, monk and abbot of Bec in Normandy, Archbishop of Canterbury, doctor of the Church, who described theology as faith seeking understanding.

19–25 April: fourth week of the Resurrection. Wed 21: in the Latin calendar, St Anselm. Fri 23: in the Latin calendar, St George. Sat 24: in the Syro-Malabar calendar, St George, Martyr (Geevarghese Sahada), an important feast. Sun 25: Fifth Sunday of Resurrection, with Mar Addai; St Mark the Evangelist (25 Apr) gives way to the Sunday this year (verify locally).
2027-04-21.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, eternal Priest according to the order of Melchizedek, King of righteousness and King of peace, you live for ever to make intercession for us. Accept the bread and wine we bring, and make them your Body and Blood. Bless our priests, who stand at the altar in your name. Make us witnesses like John, burning and shining lamps, so that the world may see in our works that the Father has sent you. Glory to you, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen. Alleluia!

kidsaint: Anselm grew up in the mountains of northern Italy. As a child he dreamed of climbing up to God's palace on the mountain top. He became a monk, a great teacher and finally Archbishop of Canterbury in England. He loved to think about God, and said that we believe so that we may understand. Lesson: you can use your mind to love God more!
2027-04-21.special: Fourth Wednesday of Resurrection. Latin calendar: St Anselm.
term: A phrase from Psalm 110:4, used by the Letter to the Hebrews for the priesthood of Christ. It is not a priesthood inherited by birth, as in the tribe of Levi, but an eternal priesthood given by God's oath. Christ is priest by who he is, the eternal Son, and he exercises it for ever as the Risen One.

family.explain: Long ago, when Abraham was coming home from a battle, a king called Melchizedek came to meet him. He brought bread and wine and blessed Abraham. He was a priest of God. The Bible says he was like a picture of Jesus. Jesus is our priest for ever. At the Holy Qurbana, bread and wine are brought to the altar, and Jesus makes them his own Body and Blood.
family.intention: We pray for our priests, and for boys whom God is calling to be priests.
family.ask: Ask: “What does our priest do for us at the Holy Qurbana? Let us thank God for him tonight.”

illus: A young engineer from Kochi, working abroad, rarely went to church. One night his father phoned from the hospital: his mother had had a stroke. He could not get a flight for two days. Unable to sleep, he found a small chapel near his apartment and sat in the back. He did not know what to pray. On the wall was a line from Hebrews: ‘He always lives to make intercession for them.’ He said later, “For the first time I understood that I did not have to find the words. Someone was already praying for my mother, and for me.” His mother recovered slowly. He still keeps a card with that verse in his wallet.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, our eternal Priest, you live for ever to intercede for us. Pray with us now, and make our prayer one with yours before the Father. Amen. Alleluia!
share: King Melchizedek of Salem brought out bread and wine (Genesis 14:18). What does the Holy Qurbana mean to me this week?
Resembling the Son of God, he remains a priest forever (Hebrews 7:3). How do I thank God for the priests in my life?
One of whom it is testified that he lives (Hebrews 7:8). Do I pray as one who believes Jesus is alive and listening?
The very works that I am doing, testify on my behalf (John 5:36). What works in my life bear witness to Christ?
pm.resp: Lord, eternal Priest, intercede for us.
interc: For our Holy Father the Pope, our Major Archbishop, our bishops and all priests, that they may serve faithfully at the altar.
For young men discerning a call to the priesthood, that they may hear and answer generously.
For those who cannot pray because of pain or despair, that Christ's intercession may carry them.
For those who seek the truth, that they may see the works of Christ in his Church and believe.
For ourselves, that we may be burning and shining lamps for Christ.
pm.close: Father, you made your Son a priest for ever according to the order of Melchizedek, and you raised him to live for ever interceding for us. Hear the prayer he makes for us, and make us faithful witnesses to him. Through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

homily: Dear friends, today the Letter to the Hebrews takes us back to a mysterious king who met Abraham with bread and wine.

Melchizedek, king of Salem, “brought out bread and wine; he was priest of God Most High.” His name means king of righteousness; Salem means peace. Scripture tells us nothing of his birth or death, so Hebrews says he resembles the Son of God and remains a priest forever. He is a picture of Christ.

Hebrews then says something full of Easter joy: the old priests were mortal, but Christ is “one of whom it is testified that he lives.” He holds his priesthood for ever, and “he always lives to make intercession” for us. Right now, the Risen Lord is praying for you before the Father.
And in every Holy Qurbana, the eternal Priest offers himself under the signs of bread and wine, as Melchizedek once foreshadowed. Our priests stand at the altar in his name.

In the Gospel Jesus calls his witnesses: John the Baptist, “a burning and shining lamp”; the works the Father gave him to do; and the Father himself. At Easter the Father gave his greatest testimony: he raised his Son from the dead.
Now it is our turn to be witnesses. Let us pray today for our priests, lean on Christ's intercession when we cannot pray, and let our works point to him. Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, long ago a king called Melchizedek brought bread and wine to Abraham and blessed him. He was a picture of Jesus, our priest for ever!
Jesus is alive and he prays for you every day. Tonight, say thank you to Jesus for praying for you!
